1900: from ἐπί and (the accusative case plural neuter of) ἐκεῖνος; upon those parts of, i.e. on the further side of:--beyond.
1901: middle voice from ἐπί and ἐκτείνω; to stretch (oneself) forward upon:--reach forth.
1902: middle voice from ἐπί and ἐνδύω; to invest upon oneself:--be clothed upon.
1903: from ἐπενδύομαι; a wrapper, i.e. outer garment:--fisher's coat.
1904: from ἐπί and ἔρχομαι; to supervene, i.e. arrive, occur, impend, attack, (figuratively) influence:--come (in, upon).
1905: from ἐπί and ἐρωτάω; to ask for, i.e. inquire, seek:--ask (after, questions), demand, desire, question.
1907: from ἐπί and ἔχω; to hold upon, i.e. (by implication) to retain; (by extension) to detain; (with implication, of νοῦς) to pay attention to:--give (take) heed unto, hold forth, mark, stay.
1908: from a comparative of ἐπί and (probably) (threats); to insult, slander:--use despitefully, falsely accuse.
1909: a primary preposition; properly, meaning superimposition (of time, place, order, etc.), as a relation of distribution (with the genitive case), i.e. over, upon, etc.; of rest (with the dative case) at, on, etc.; of direction (with the accusative case) towards, upon, etc.:--about (the times), above, after, against, among, as long as (touching), at, beside, X have charge of, (be-, (where-))fore, in (a place, as much as, the time of, -to), (because) of, (up-)on (behalf of), over, (by, for) the space of, through(-out), (un-)to(-ward), with. In compounds it retains essentially the same import, at, upon, etc. (literally or figuratively).
1910: from ἐπί and the base of βάσις; to walk upon, i.e. mount, ascend, embark, arrive:--come (into), enter into, go abroad, sit upon, take ship.
1911: from ἐπί and βάλλω; to throw upon (literal or figurative, transitive or reflexive; usually with more or less force); specially (with ἑαυτοῦ implied) to reflect; impersonally, to belong to:--beat into, cast (up-)on, fall, lay (on), put (unto), stretch forth, think on.
1912: from ἐπί and βαρέω; to be heavy upon, i.e. (pecuniarily) to be expensive to; figuratively, to be severe towards:--be chargeable to, overcharge.
1913: from ἐπί and a reduplicated derivative of the base of βάσις (compare ἀναβιβάζω); to cause to mount (an animal):--set on.
1914: from ἐπί and βλέπω; to gaze at (with favor, pity or partiality):--look upon, regard, have respect to.
1916: from ἐπί and βοάω; to exclaim against:--cry.
1917: from a presumed compound of ἐπί and βούλομαι; a plan against someone, i.e. a plot:--laying (lying) in wait.
1918: from ἐπί and a derivative of γάμος; to form affinity with, i.e. (specially) in a levirate way:--marry.
1919: from ἐπί and γῆ; worldly (physically or morally):--earthly, in earth, terrestrial.
1920: from ἐπί and γίνομαι; to arrive upon, i.e. spring up (as a wind):--blow.
1921: from ἐπί and γινώσκω; to know upon some mark, i.e. recognize; by implication, to become fully acquainted with, to acknowledge:--(ac-, have, take)know(-ledge, well), perceive.
1922: from ἐπιγινώσκω; recognition, i.e. (by implication) full discernment, acknowledgement:--(ac-)knowledge(-ing, - ment).
1924: from ἐπί and γράφω; to inscribe (physically or mentally):--inscription, write in (over, thereon).
1925: from ἐπί and δεικνύω; to exhibit (physically or mentally):--shew.
1926: from ἐπί and δέχομαι; to admit (as a guest or (figuratively) teacher):--receive.
1927: from a compound of ἐπί and δῆμος; to make oneself at home, i.e. (by extension) to reside (in a foreign country):--(be) dwelling (which were) there, stranger.
1928: middle voice from ἐπί and διατάσσω; to appoint besides, i.e. supplement (as a codicil):--add to.
1929: from ἐπί and δίδωμι; to give over (by hand or surrender):--deliver unto, give, let (+ (her drive)), offer.
1930: from ἐπί and a derivative of ὀρθός; to straighten further, i.e. (figuratively) arrange additionally:--set in order.
1931: from ἐπί and δύνω; to set fully (as the sun):--go down.
1932: from ἐπιεικής; suitableness, i.e. (by implication) equity, mildness:--clemency, gentleness.
1933: from ἐπί and εἴκω; appropriate, i.e. (by implication) mild:--gentle, moderation, patient.
1934: from ἐπί and ζητέω; to search (inquire) for; intensively, to demand, to crave:--desire, enquire, seek (after, for).
1935: from ἐπί and θάνατος; doomed to death:--appointed to death.
1936: from ἐπιτίθημι; an imposition (of hands officially):--laying (putting) on.
1937: from ἐπί and θυμός; to set the heart upon, i.e. long for (rightfully or otherwise):--covet, desire, would fain, lust (after).
1938: from ἐπιθυμέω; a craver:--+ lust after.
1939: from ἐπιθυμέω; a longing (especially for what is forbidden):--concupiscence, desire, lust (after).
1940: from ἐπί and καθίζω; to seat upon:--set on.
1941: middle voice from ἐπί and καλέω; to entitle; by implication, to invoke (for aid, worship, testimony, decision, etc.):--appeal (unto), call (on, upon), surname.
1942: from ἐπικαλύπτω; a covering, i.e. (figuratively) pretext:--cloke.
1943: from ἐπί and καλύπτω; to conceal, i.e. (figuratively) forgive:--cover.
1944: from ἐπί and a derivative of καταράομαι; imprecated, i.e. execrable:--accursed.
1945: from ἐπί and κεῖμαι; to rest upon (literally or figuratively):--impose, be instant, (be) laid (there-, up-)on, (when) lay (on), lie (on), press upon.
1946: from (compare ἐπικουρία) (a noted philosopher); an Epicurean or follower of Epicurus:--Epicurean.
1947: from a compound of ἐπί and a (prolonged) form of the base of κοράσιον (in the sense of servant); assistance:--help.
1948: from ἐπί and κρίνω; to adjudge:--give sentence.
1949: middle voice from ἐπί and λαμβάνω; to seize (for help, injury, attainment, or any other purpose; literally or figuratively):--catch, lay hold (up-)on, take (by, hold of, on).
1950: middle voice from ἐπί and λανθάνω; to lose out of mind; by implication, to neglect:--(be) forget(-ful of).
1951: middle voice from ἐπί and λέγω; to surname, select:--call, choose.
1952: from ἐπί and λείπω; to leave upon, i.e. (figuratively) to be insufficient for:--fail.
1953: from a derivative of ἐπιλανθάνομαι; negligence:--X forgetful.
1954: from ἐπί and λοιποί; left over, i.e. remaining:--rest.
1956: from ἐπί and λύω; to solve further, i.e. (figuratively) to explain, decide:--determine, expound.
1957: from ἐπί and μαρτυρέω; to attest further, i.e. corroborate:--testify.
1958: from ἐπιμελέομαι; carefulness, i.e. kind attention (hospitality):--+ refresh self.
1959: middle voice from ἐπί and the same as μέλω; to care for (physically or otherwise):--take care of.
1960: adverb from a derivative of ἐπιμελέομαι; carefully:--diligently.
1961: from ἐπί and μένω; to stay over, i.e. remain (figuratively, persevere):--abide (in), continue (in), tarry.
1962: from ἐπί and νεύω; to nod at, i.e. (by implication) to assent:--consent.
1963: from ἐπί and νοῦς; attention of the mind, i.e. (by implication) purpose:--thought.
1964: from ἐπίορκος; to commit perjury:--forswear self.
1965: from ἐπί and ὅρκος; on oath, i.e. (falsely) a forswearer:--perjured person.
1966: feminine singular participle of a comparative of ἐπί and (to go); supervening, i.e. (ἡμέρα or νύξ being expressed or implied) the ensuing day or night:--following, next.
1967: perhaps from the same as ἐπιοῦσα; tomorrow's; but more probably from ἐπί and a derivative of the present participle feminine of εἰμί; for subsistence, i.e. needful:--daily.
1968: from ἐπί and πίπτω; to embrace (with affection) or seize (with more or less violence; literally or figuratively):--fall into (on, upon) lie on, press upon.
1969: from ἐπί and πλήσσω; to chastise, i.e. (with words) to upbraid:--rebuke.
1970: from ἐπί and πνίγω; to throttle upon, i.e. (figuratively) overgrow:--choke.
1971: from ἐπί and potheo (to yearn); to dote upon, i.e. intensely crave possession (lawfully or wrongfully):--(earnestly) desire (greatly), (greatly) long (after), lust.
1972: from ἐπιποθέω; a longing for:--earnest (vehement) desire.
1973: from ἐπί and a derivative of the latter part of ἐπιποθέω; yearned upon, i.e. greatly loved:--longed for.
1975: from ἐπί and πορεύομαι; to journey further, i.e. travel on (reach):--come.
1976: from ἐπί and the base of ῥαφίς; to stitch upon, i.e. fasten with the needle:--sew on.
1977: from ἐπί and ῥίπτω; to throw upon (literally or figuratively):--cast upon.
1978: from ἐπί and some form of the base of σημαίνω; remarkable, i.e. (figuratively) eminent:--notable, of note.
1979: from a compound of ἐπί and a derivative of σῖτος; a provisioning, i.e. (concretely) food:--victuals.
1980: middle voice from ἐπί and the base of σκοπός; to inspect, i.e. (by implication) to select; by extension, to go to see, relieve:--look out, visit.
1981: from ἐπί and σκηνόω; to tent upon, i.e. (figuratively) abide with :--rest upon.
1982: from ἐπί and a derivative of σκιά; to cast a shade upon, i.e. (by analogy) to envelop in a haze of brilliancy; figuratively, to invest with preternatural influence:--overshadow.
1983: from ἐπί and σκοπέω; to oversee; by implication, to beware:--look diligently, take the oversight.
1984: from ἐπισκέπτομαι; inspection (for relief); by implication, superintendence; specially, the Christian "episcopate":--the office of a "bishop", bishoprick, visitation.
1985: from ἐπί and σκοπός (in the sense of ἐπισκοπέω); a superintendent, i.e. Christian officer in genitive case charge of a (or the) church (literally or figuratively):--bishop, overseer.
1986: from ἐπί and σπάω; to draw over, i.e. (with ἀκροβυστία implied) efface the mark of circumcision (by recovering with the foreskin):--become uncircumcised.
1987: apparently a middle voice of ἐφίστημι (with νοῦς implied); to put the mind upon, i.e. comprehend, or be acquainted with:--know, understand.
1988: from ἐπί and a presumed derivative of ἵστημι; an appointee over, i.e. commander (teacher):--master.
1989: from ἐπί and στέλλω; to enjoin (by writing), i.e. (genitive case) to communicate by letter (for any purpose):--write (a letter, unto).
1991: from ἐπί and στηρίζω; to support further, i.e. reestablish:--confirm, strengthen.
1992: from ἐπιστέλλω; a written message:--"epistle," letter.
1993: from ἐπί and στόμα; to put something over the mouth, i.e. (figuratively) to silence:--stop mouths.
1994: from ἐπί and στρέφω; to revert (literally, figuratively or morally):--come (go) again, convert, (re-)turn (about, again).
1995: from ἐπιστρέφω; reversion, i.e. morally, revolution:--conversion.
1996: from ἐπί and συνάγω; to collect upon the same place:--gather (together).
1997: from ἐπισυνάγω; a complete collection; especially a Christian meeting (for worship):--assembling (gathering) together.
1998: from ἐπί and συντρέχω; to hasten together upon one place (or a particular occasion):--come running together.
1999: from the middle voice of a compound of ἐπί and συνιστάω; a conspiracy, i.e. concourse (riotous or friendly):--that which cometh upon, + raising up.
